anomaly_def.Name: Replication Synchronization Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description: Definition: Root cause located in the replication pipeline, where standbys, read replicas, subscribers, or downstream change-data consumers cannot receive, persist, or apply transaction-log records at the rate the primary produces them. It is distinct from the local log subsystem and from storage anomalies because the failure surface is the cross-node receive and apply path rather than the primary's own write path. Observable phenomena: widening log-position gaps reported by replication-state monitoring views, increasing receive, write, flush, and replay lag, growing relay logs or retained primary log segments, stale reads on replicas, reduced failover readiness, and primary-side disk usage growing because replication-state objects prevent log recycling. Possible contributing factors: insufficient network bandwidth or excessive latency between primary and replica, replica CPU or I/O incapable of replaying redo at the source rate, single-threaded or under-parallelized apply processes, oversized transactions or schema-change operations applied as a single unit, schema or index differences between primary and replica, apply-side lock conflicts, replication filtering or conflict-resolution errors, and disconnected or paused consumers whose retention objects remain active.

entry.official_description: CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO ASSIGN_GTIDS_TO_ANONYMOUS_TRANSACTIONS = <UUID> cannot be executed because the UUID value is equal to the group_replication_view_change_uuid.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with log shipping, replica apply state, replication-channel configuration, or cross-node communication needed to keep replicated state consistent.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect replication channel health, sender/receiver state, log retention, downstream apply lag, and network stability between replication endpoints.
